Not quite. Not every apps obeys this and I’m not even sure how. Adobe’s apps all insist on creating an “Adobe” folder in your iCloud-synced Documents folder regardless of file system permissions. You may deny access to every Adobe app under the sun, and they will still create those goddamned folders at launch. Apple’s solutions are not universally implemented and are most definitely not universally obeyed. The day Apple gives me a way to simply say “fuck you Adobe, you won’t have access to my Documents folder anymore” is the day that these permission models have started to work properly, until then it’s all theatre.

hi HN - i'm Francesco, founder of Cua. Since we released Lume almost 2 years ago ( https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42908061 ) we've used it to run agents and CI on macOS. In order to meet our customer demands for evals, and RL at scale, we decided to build our own vmm on Hypervisor.framework. We call it Hoy, and it provides faster boot time to ssh and faster resetting of VMs between runs (on the same M4 Pro: boot 5.3 s vs 6.6 s, restore 1.2 s vs 3.0 s with Apple's Virtualization framework), as well as better compatibility with graphic design software requiring gpu, and a gpu renderer path for running local models at close to native speed. We're releasing it for free, including commercial use. closed-source to start with. some limits: two macOS VMs per Mac, enforced to meet apple's macOS license, and no iCloud sign-in yet.
